change_summary: Asperger's Disorder was eliminated as a standalone diagnosis and merged into a single Autism Spectrum Disorder category with severity levels.
clinical_rationale: Research showed no reliable clinical distinction between Asperger's, PDD-NOS, and autistic disorder; a spectrum model improved diagnostic consistency.
current_criteria_summary: Autism Spectrum Disorder is diagnosed based on persistent deficits in social communication/interaction plus restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, rated across three severity levels.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Autism Spectrum Disorder, 2013

change_summary: PDD-NOS was folded into Autism Spectrum Disorder as a single unified diagnosis.
clinical_rationale: Same rationale as Asperger's merge — spectrum model replaced separate subtypes.
current_criteria_summary: See Autism Spectrum Disorder criteria — spectrum-based severity rating replacing separate subtype labels.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Autism Spectrum Disorder, 2013

change_summary: Eliminated as a separate diagnosis, absorbed into Autism Spectrum Disorder.
clinical_rationale: Consolidation of autism-related subtypes under one spectrum model.
current_criteria_summary: See Autism Spectrum Disorder criteria.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Autism Spectrum Disorder, 2013

change_summary: All schizophrenia subtypes (paranoid, catatonic, disorganized, undifferentiated, residual) were removed; schizophrenia is now diagnosed as a single condition with symptom dimension ratings.
clinical_rationale: Subtypes showed poor reliability and limited treatment or prognostic value in longitudinal studies.
current_criteria_summary: Schizophrenia is diagnosed via core symptom criteria (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, etc.) rated on severity dimensions rather than subtype.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Schizophrenia Spectrum, 2013

change_summary: Catatonic subtype removed; catatonia is now a specifier that can apply across multiple diagnoses, not a schizophrenia subtype.
clinical_rationale: Catatonia occurs across many conditions, not just schizophrenia — reclassifying it as a specifier improved diagnostic accuracy.
current_criteria_summary: Catatonia specifier applied when relevant motor/behavioral symptoms are present.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Schizophrenia Spectrum, 2013

change_summary: The 'bereavement exclusion' was removed — grief no longer automatically rules out an MDD diagnosis if criteria are otherwise met.
clinical_rationale: Evidence showed grief-triggered depression can be clinically significant and undertreated if automatically excluded.
current_criteria_summary: MDD can be diagnosed even in the context of recent bereavement if full symptom criteria and duration are met, with clinical judgment distinguishing normal grief from disorder.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Depressive Disorders, 2013

change_summary: Substance Abuse and Substance Dependence were merged into a single Substance Use Disorder diagnosis with severity ratings (mild/moderate/severe).
clinical_rationale: The abuse/dependence split had weak empirical support; a single severity-graded disorder better reflected clinical presentation.
current_criteria_summary: Substance Use Disorder is diagnosed via 11 criteria with severity determined by symptom count (2-3=mild, 4-5=moderate, 6+=severe).
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Substance-Related Disorders, 2013

change_summary: Renamed from Gender Identity Disorder to Gender Dysphoria, shifting focus from identity as pathology to the distress caused by incongruence.
clinical_rationale: Reduces stigma by framing distress, not identity itself, as the clinical concern.
current_criteria_summary: Gender Dysphoria focuses on clinically significant distress related to incongruence between experienced and assigned gender.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Gender Dysphoria, 2013

change_summary: Terminology updated; diagnostic focus shifted to include adaptive functioning alongside IQ scores.
clinical_rationale: Reduces stigma; better reflects real-world functional impact beyond IQ score alone.
current_criteria_summary: Intellectual Disability diagnosed via deficits in intellectual functioning AND adaptive functioning across conceptual, social, and practical domains.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Intellectual Disability, 2013

new_label: Somatic Symptom Disorder / Illness Anxiety Disorder
change_summary: Hypochondriasis was split into two diagnoses depending on presence of somatic symptoms.
clinical_rationale: Better differentiates patients with predominant physical symptoms vs predominant health anxiety without significant symptoms.
current_criteria_summary: Somatic Symptom Disorder involves distressing physical symptoms with excessive thoughts/behaviors; Illness Anxiety Disorder involves high health anxiety with minimal/no somatic symptoms.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Somatic Symptom Disorders, 2013

change_summary: New diagnosis added specifically to address overdiagnosis of pediatric bipolar disorder in children with chronic irritability.
clinical_rationale: Addressed a documented pattern of children being misdiagnosed with bipolar disorder for chronic temper outbursts.
current_criteria_summary: DMDD is diagnosed in children with severe recurrent temper outbursts plus persistently irritable mood, distinct from episodic bipolar mood changes.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Depressive Disorders, 2013

change_summary: Elevated from an example under 'Eating Disorder NOS' in DSM-IV to a fully recognized standalone diagnosis.
clinical_rationale: Recognized as a distinct, prevalent condition requiring its own diagnostic criteria and treatment approach.
current_criteria_summary: Binge Eating Disorder involves recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food with loss of control, without regular compensatory behaviors, at defined frequency/duration thresholds.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Feeding and Eating Disorders, 2013

change_summary: ICD-11 introduced Complex PTSD as a distinct diagnosis from PTSD, capturing effects of prolonged, repeated trauma.
clinical_rationale: Clinical evidence showed prolonged/repeated trauma (e.g., childhood abuse) produces a distinguishable symptom pattern beyond standard PTSD criteria.
current_criteria_summary: Complex PTSD includes core PTSD symptoms plus disturbances in self-organization: emotional regulation difficulty, negative self-concept, and relationship difficulties.
source_citation: World Health Organization, ICD-11 for Mortality and Morbidity Statistics, 2019/2022

change_summary: Moved out of the 'Mental and Behavioural Disorders' chapter entirely into a new 'Conditions Related to Sexual Health' chapter.
clinical_rationale: Reflects evidence that gender incongruence itself is not a mental disorder, reducing stigma while retaining access to care coding.
current_criteria_summary: Gender Incongruence is classified under sexual health, not mental disorders, focused on marked incongruence between experienced gender and assigned sex.
source_citation: World Health Organization, ICD-11 for Mortality and Morbidity Statistics, 2019/2022

change_summary: New behavioral addiction diagnosis added to ICD-11, not present in ICD-10.
clinical_rationale: Growing clinical and research evidence of impaired control over gaming behavior causing significant functional impairment.
current_criteria_summary: Gaming Disorder involves impaired control over gaming, increasing priority over other activities, and continuation despite negative consequences, for at least 12 months.
source_citation: World Health Organization, ICD-11 for Mortality and Morbidity Statistics, 2019/2022

change_summary: The term 'ADD' was officially retired; it is now classified as a specific presentation type under the broader ADHD diagnosis.
clinical_rationale: Research showed that inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity are dimensions of the same underlying spectrum, not entirely separate disorders.
current_criteria_summary: ADHD is diagnosed via a persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning, specified by presentation type.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: ADHD, 2013

change_summary: Renamed to Social Anxiety Disorder to reflect that the condition is broader and more functionally impairing than a simple 'phobia'.
clinical_rationale: The term 'phobia' minimized the severe, pervasive impact this anxiety has on a person's entire social and professional life.
current_criteria_summary: Social Anxiety Disorder involves marked fear or anxiety about one or more social situations where the individual is exposed to possible scrutiny by others.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Anxiety Disorders, 2013

change_summary: The term 'Dementia' was replaced with 'Major Neurocognitive Disorder' to reduce stigma and focus on the specific brain pathology.
clinical_rationale: 'Dementia' carries severe negative stigma and was often incorrectly used as a catch-all; the new term requires specifying the exact cause (e.g., Alzheimer's, Traumatic Brain Injury).
current_criteria_summary: Major Neurocognitive Disorder is diagnosed by evidence of significant cognitive decline from a previous level of performance in one or more cognitive domains.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Neurocognitive Disorders, 2013

change_summary: Burnout was specifically upgraded and detailed as an 'occupational phenomenon' rather than a medical condition or generic stress.
clinical_rationale: Clarified that burnout specifically refers to chronic workplace stress that has not been successfully managed, preventing it from being misdiagnosed as generalized depression.
current_criteria_summary: Burnout is a syndrome conceptualized as resulting from chronic workplace stress, characterized by exhaustion, increased mental distance from one's job, and reduced professional efficacy.
source_citation: World Health Organization, ICD-11 for Mortality and Morbidity Statistics, 2019/2022

new_label: Bipolar II Disorder / MDD with Mixed Features
change_summary: Added 'with mixed features' specifier to MDD and clarified criteria separating unipolar depression from Bipolar II.
clinical_rationale: Over 60% of bipolar patients are initially misdiagnosed with unipolar depression; updating criteria for subthreshold hypomanic symptoms helps identify bipolarity earlier.
keywords_for_matching: unipolar depression;major depressive disorder;clinical depression;depressive episode
current_criteria_summary: Bipolar II and MDD with mixed features require evaluating past or current hypomanic symptoms (decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, rapid speech) alongside depressive episodes.
source_citation: American Psychiatric Association, DSM-5 Fact Sheet: Mood Disorders, 2013
